summary_of_reasoning: No defect found in the pinned Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 contracts' position-derived parameters. Checked end to end: (1) ArbitrationConstants (LEVELS=2, log2step [38,0], height [54,38]) tile the 92-bit meta-cycle space exactly (24+48+20 from the regenerated EmulatorConstants); height(1)=log2step(0)-log2step(1). (2) Commitment.toCycle(startCycle + pos<<log2step) and the leaf convention (leaf p = state after transition startCycle+p, agree state = leaf p-1 or initialHash) agree with CartesiStateTransition ('counter indexes the output leaf; machineState is its predecessor'), with the inner tournament's startCycle = toCycle(divergencePosition) and initialHash = agreeHash, and with the inner tournament's last leaf = parent leaf p. (3) CartesiStateTransition derives the form from the counter alone: counter & (2^68-1)==0 -> provider root for input counter>>68 (zero -> plain uarch step; nonzero -> SendCmioResponse with revertRootHash = machineState (A4) then step); counter & (2^20-1)==2^20-1 -> step+reset; else step; counter >= 2^92 rejected. The two masks never overlap. (4) DaveConsensus.provideMerkleRootOfInput returns 0 exactly past the sealed upper bound, which is capped at 2^24 = MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH, checks keccak of the bytes against InputBox, and builds the root with log2 size max(ceilLog2(len),5), the same height SendCmioResponse/emulator derive (zero padding included). The provider reads the current epoch bounds, but a root tournament cannot finish (and the epoch cannot advance) while any child match is alive: a sealed inner match has two paused clocks with positive allowance, so classifyTimeoutAt is NONE and only win/eliminateInnerTournament (which require a finished child) delete it. (5) Leaves only at height zero of the full tree: joinTournament uses getRootForLastLeaf with siblings.length == height; sealDivergence authenticates the agree state with requireState(height, divergencePosition-1) with exactly height siblings, against the commitment whose turn it is (height-parity rule verified: revealer is one iff height odd); bisection invariant (otherParent = revealer's node, leftNode/rightNode = waiting side's children, they differ) holds, so the bisection converges on the leftmost divergent leaf and position += 1<<(h-1) on right descent is correct. (6) The outputs-root extraction (LibMachineValidityProof/LibLeafProof) authenticates iflags_Y, htif_tohost and the first tx-buffer leaf at height 0 of the 59-level tree, all against the same root; it imports EmulatorConstants from solidity-step 0.15.0, but every constant it uses (0x308, 0x330, 0x60800000, 63, HTIF masks/reasons, isYieldedManualWith) is identical to the regenerated step. Output proofs fix 63 siblings and index < 2^63. (7) The recipe referee (prt.lua) mirrors Dave's validators (claim proof at last leaf, height-0 target, sibling count == tournament height, seal proof at leaf_index-1); its keccak is cartesi.keccak256, whose two-argument form refuses non-32-byte arguments, so verify_slice cannot be fooled with length-shifted node splits. The bridge maps baseCycle + (divergencePosition << log2Stride) and splits cycle into (input>>68, period, offset) consistently, and prt-epoch.lua assigns inputs to epochs exactly as DaveConsensus seals them (log order, 2^24 cap).

candidates.title: Recipe referee model assigns an unbounded input record to one epoch (no cap at the input limit per epoch), so inputs past 2^24 are unaddressable and crash the honest player
candidates.component: PRT referee model in doc/recipes (prt.lua: new_dapp_contract, run_epoch, validate_state_transition_response); honest player add_pending_input (support)
candidates.role: Referee model (prt.lua referee); the crashing player is Support standing in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua new_dapp_contract (lines ~850-861: inputs = map(input_paths, fs.read_file), no length check), run_epoch (lines ~805-810: publishes every input and seals with #dapp_contract.inputs), validate_state_transition_response (line ~277: dapp_contract.inputs[epoch_input_offset + 1], epoch_input_offset < 2^24 by geometry), player add_pending_input (line ~2211: assert(epoch_input_offset < 1 << LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH))
candidates.description: The model's dapp contract takes every input file it is given as the epoch's input record and announces all of them, sealing the epoch with #inputs. Nothing caps the record at 2^ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH = 2^24, unlike DaveConsensus (MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH, excess stays pending for later epochs). The dispute grid can only address input slots 0..2^24-1 (mcycle_height = 24+48-p), so inputs at offset >= 2^24 are assigned to the epoch by the record but never delivered by any transition form the referee derives. The honest player asserts on the first such input_added event and stops computing its claim. This contradicts A3 ('The input record assigns no more inputs to an epoch than the input limit per epoch') and Dave's behavior, and the manual's list of model simplifications (README ~11308) does not mention it.
candidates.trigger: Whoever supplies the referee's input record: the referee CLI caller (input file paths), or a Lua caller of the referee entry points, with more than 2^24 inputs for one epoch.
candidates.reachability: Not reachable through the documented CLI: 2^24+1 paths exceed the exec argument limit (ARG_MAX), so it needs a Lua-level caller or a modified launcher. In the model the input record is the referee's own configuration, not something an input sender controls, unlike Dave's InputBox.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is the deployment's input record exceeding the limit, which by itself would be excluded ('Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8'), but the exclusion does not apply 'unless an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)', and here the referee model is what assigns the oversized record. In scope. 2. Role: prt.lua's referee is the 'Referee model' (AUDIT.md table). 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it.' The player crash is Support. 3. High/Medium cases: none of the listed cases fits. 4. Critical? It violates A3 ('The input record assigns no more inputs to an epoch than the input limit per epoch') and stops the honest player (R4: 'It assigns inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3)'). Rated as a deployed referee whose input record the adversary fills ('Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts'), it would be Critical: the honest claim goes undefended and any claim can win. But in this model the input record is the trusted referee's command-line configuration, and the CLI cannot carry 2^24+1 paths. Under that reading it is 5. Low (a real defect reachable only by misuse of the model's trusted configuration). Which reading applies depends on whether triage treats the model's input files as the adversary-fed on-chain input record. Claimed: Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: A deployed referee with this behavior would let inputs beyond the epoch limit fall out of the verified history while the honest operator, which applies the limit, refuses the epoch. That is a completeness failure in which any claim could win. In the demonstration model it only shows a divergence from Dave and from A3 that the manual does not list as a simplification.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only. Did not run: the trigger needs 2^24+1 inputs.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: load prt.lua's referee pieces with fs.read_file stubbed (or one tiny file repeated) and a dapp contract of 2^24+1 inputs, run run_epoch against a recording stub server, and assert that the epoch_sealed count is <= 2^24 (or that new_dapp_contract refuses the record). Exit 1 on audit/prt2, where the count is 2^24+1.

candidates.title: Manual's referee model restricts uarch-tournament joins to holders of the two disputed mcycle claims; Dave lets any address join an inner tournament
candidates.location: doc/README.md 'Settling a match' ('Only holders of the two disputed claims may join, and a uarch claim must end at one of the two contested states, as validContestedFinalState requires on chain'); doc/recipes/prt.lua open_uarch_tournament (requests claims only from subscription_hash of the two mcycle claims); Dave Tournament.sol joinTournament (any msg.sender, only validContestedFinalState checked)
candidates.description: The normative model accepts uarch claims only from holders of the two contested mcycle claims. The deployed referee accepts a join from anyone whose last leaf is a contested final state. The manual's list of simplifications does not cover this, so THREAT_MODEL section 5 ('Any other disagreement between a deployed referee and the model is a defect in one of the two') makes it a defect in one of them. This is outside A2 proper (it is A1-adjacent); reported because it is a referee-model disagreement found while checking leaf authentication.
candidates.trigger: Any party that joins a Dave inner tournament without having posted or held either disputed mcycle commitment.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on any deployment: inner tournaments are open to any caller with the bond.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No exclusion applies. 2. Role: both components are the referee model. Section 3: 'a disagreement between the two on what a referee verifies or derives is a defect in one of them, rated as if the manual were right'. 3. High/Medium: no listed case fits. 4. Critical? Rated as if the manual were right, Dave accepts extra joiners. A1 holds in Dave ('A uarch-level claim counts only if its last leaf, authenticated as in A2, is one of the two states that its enclosing match disagrees on'), and the adversary can already 'Hold any claim, including the honest one, and answer for it', so becoming a holder costs it nothing. No rule or obligation is violated at a reachable state. 5. Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None found. It is a model/deployment discrepancy that the manual should either list as a simplification or align with Dave.
candidates.test_idea: None needed beyond documentation: a contract test that joins a child tournament from a fresh address with a contested final state shows Dave accepts it, while the manual says only holders may join.
